title: Color / Optical Adjustment
slide_intent: Judge colors in their actual adjacency because isolated swatches can appear different when they touch.
strategic_value: Adjusting adjacent hues can help Google preserve the perceived brightness of its familiar palette in a compact G.
demonstration: Four separated labeled swatches move together; green, yellow and red change while blue remains stable, ending with a brighter adjacent palette.
practical_value: Compare both isolated and touching colors before transferring a wordmark palette into a compact symbol.

content_islands.name: Separated swatches
content_islands.spec: Align blue, green, yellow and red rectangles with white gaps and small names and hex labels.

content_islands.name: Adjacent comparison
content_islands.spec: Close the gaps and animate the color adjustment in place so the changed hues can be compared.

reference_purposes.Intent: The article explains that adjacent hues can optically darken, prompting increased vibrancy in red, green and yellow.
reference_purposes.Expression: The clip presents the four-color family as separated and contiguous fields.
reference_purposes.Application: The transition demonstrates testing and adjusting the colors in adjacency.

ingredient.name: Adjacent four-color palette
ingredient.role: Keep the four hues visually distinct and bright when they share boundaries.
ingredient.application: Evaluate adjoining hues together; this example increases the vibrancy of red, green and yellow while retaining blue.
ingredient.scope: The 2015 identity comparison, especially the compact G. This is not a general instruction to alter approved brand colors.
